intro.en: Ways to pay, seasonal sales, and everyday expressions about money.

estar sin blanca.en: to be broke; to have no money

nota.en: Colloquial. Blanca was also the name of a historical coin; the expression means having no money.

costar un ojo de la cara.en: to cost an arm and a leg
costar un ojo de la cara.pron: kos-TAR un O-ho de la KA-ra

nota.en: Colloquial. Tirado agrees with the item: el precio está tirado, la chaqueta está tirada.

apretarse el cinturón.en: to tighten one's belt; to cut back

nota.en: The reflexive pronoun agrees with the subject: me aprieto el cinturón, nos apretamos el cinturón.

tirar la casa por la ventana.en: to spend lavishly; to spare no expense
tirar la casa por la ventana.pron: ti-RAR la KA-sa por la ben-TA-na

nota.en: Informal and critical. Use agarrado for a man and agarrada for a woman.
In no mirar el dinero, the negative phrase means not to worry about the cost.

la ganga.en: the bargain; a very good deal

al contado.en: in full; paid all at once

nota.en: The adjective agrees with the person: tacaño, tacaña, tacaños, tacañas.
The adjective agrees with the person: derrochador, derrochadora, derrochadores, derrochadoras.
The adjective agrees with the person: ahorrador, ahorradora, ahorradores, ahorradoras.

las tres bes.en: the three Bs: good, pretty and cheap

nota.en: A playful shopping slogan: bueno, bonito y barato.

texto.en:
How you pay: **en efectivo**, **con tarjeta**, **a plazos**, or **al contado** (in full).

**Las rebajas** are seasonal sale periods; dates vary. You may see **un descuento del 30 %**, **una oferta** or **una ganga**. A good buy has **las tres bes**: **bueno, bonito y barato** (good, pretty and cheap).

Common informal expressions: **estar sin blanca** means to have no money; **costar un ojo de la cara** means to be very expensive; **estar tirado** means to be very cheap. **Apretarse el cinturón** means to cut back, while **tirar la casa por la ventana** means to spend lavishly. **Ser un agarrado/a** means to be stingy and can sound critical. **Mirar el dinero** means to watch one's spending; **no mirar el dinero** means not to worry about the cost.

Related descriptions: **tacaño/a** (stingy), **derrochador/a** (a big spender), **ahorrador/a** (thrifty; a saver).

frases.es: Estoy sin blanca. Este mes tengo que apretarme el cinturón.
frases.en: I'm broke. This month I have to tighten my belt.

frases.es: Pues mira estos zapatos. Están tirados: veinte euros.
frases.en: Well, look at these shoes. They're dirt cheap: twenty euros.

frases.es: Los otros me gustan más, pero cuestan un ojo de la cara.
frases.en: I like the other ones more, but they cost an arm and a leg.
analisis: cuestan un ojo de la cara

frases.es: ¡Qué agarrada eres! Yo, en rebajas, tiro la casa por la ventana.
frases.en: You're so stingy! I spare no expense during the sales.
analisis: tiro la casa por la ventana

frases.es: Claro, tú pagas con tarjeta y no miras el dinero.
frases.en: Of course, you pay by card and don't worry about the cost.

frases.es: Y tú ahorras tanto que nunca compras nada.
frases.en: And you save so much that you never buy anything.

texto.en:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about how you manage your money: what you spend most on and where you could save.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Explain to a friend aloud why you cannot lend them money, or agree with conditions.
